reader.requirement: At --std 85 a relation that compares a numeric operand with a nonnumeric operand (elementary alphanumeric, alphabetic, numeric-edited, or a group) must be refused unless the numeric operand is an integer data item or integer literal of the same usage (DISPLAY) as the nonnumeric operand; noninteger (V or leading-P scaled) items, noninteger literals, COMPUTATIONAL items and arithmetic expressions opposite a nonnumeric operand are refused, and the admitted pairs compare as characters.

edition-consulted.switches: data.Edition.Permissive (the --permissive dialect flag, not the edition) turns COBOL2532 into a warning; same at every --std

reader.edition-search: grep CobolVersion|Edition.Edition|DialectLevel|Std in RelationComparability.cs and IntrinsicArgumentRules.cs: none; the only switch in CheckGeneralRelationComparability is Permissive. The path is edition-blind, and the 2023 rule (8.8.4.2.5 integer of usage display or national) coincides with the 1985 text because 1985 has no national usage.
reader.witnesses-cover: part: the witnesses exercise function operands and defined pairs; not exercised: leading-P noninteger item, noninteger literal, COMP integer against a group or numeric-edited operand

probes.printed: COBOL2532 on all nine relations: 9V9 vs X(3) both orders, 9(3) COMP vs X(3), PP99 vs X(3), X(3) = 1.5, X(3) = NC + 1, ZZ9 = COMP, group = COMP, group = 9V9 (one unrelated COBOL0900 for a numeric VALUE on a numeric-edited item, correct at 85)
probes.expected: each refused: noninteger numeric vs nonnumeric, or usage differs, or not an integer data item/literal

probes.printed: A-EQ B-EQ C-EQ D-NE E-NE F-EQ G-NE H-GE
probes.expected: 9(3)=7 vs '007' equal both orders and vs group; ZZ9 '  7' vs 007 not equal; '007' = 7 compares '7  ' not equal; '007' = 007 equal; ZERO vs 9(3)=7 numeric not equal; 'ABC' < 007 false in native collating

citations.check: OK  §1985:VI.6.3.1.1.2 SR3  (6.3.1.1.2 Comparison of Nonnumeric Operands)  the text is in SR3 [A noninteger numeric operand cannot be compared to a nonnumeric operand]
OK  §1985:VI.6.3.1.1.2 SR3  the text is in SR3 [Numeric and nonnumeric operands may be compared only when their usage is the same]
OK  §1985:VI.6.3.1.1.2  the text is in the clause [it must be an integer data item or an integer literal]

reader.notes: The one comparability table refuses every noninteger, non-DISPLAY or expression numeric operand opposite a character-class operand (group included, as class alphanumeric) with COBOL2532 at --std 85, and the admitted integer DISPLAY pairs run with the character comparison of the numeric item's image. Side observation, not this rule: DISPLAY of PIC 9V9 prints '1.5', which docs/conformance/7/DOC-A.1-56.md records as the --numeric-display decimal default (owner decision PB3467).

refuter.evidence: Probes under E:/COBOL-coord/scratch/coderead-1985/out/refute-1985-061/. q1ref.cob (--compile-only, --std 85): FUNCTION LENGTH(AX) = AX, FUNCTION ORD("A") = AX, FUNCTION INTEGER(1.5) = AX, AX = FUNCTION MOD(7 3), AX = -1.5 each draw COBOL2532; IX = AX (index-name) and IXD = AX (index data item) draw COBOL2533 (the 6.3.1.1.3 pairing rule). Integer functions are refused, consistent with §1985:IV.4.3.8.3.3 SR4 (an integer function 'may be used only in an arithmetic expression', and the 1985 text requires an integer DATA ITEM or integer literal opposite a nonnumeric operand). q1run.cob (run): signed integer DISPLAY admitted against alphanumeric with the 1985 MOVE semantics the rule points to (§1985:VI.6.19.4 GR4a, sign not moved and a separate sign not counted): S9(3) SIGN LEADING SEPARATE -7 = '007 ' EQ, = '-007' NE, = X(3) '007' EQ (space extension); trailing-overpunch S9(3) -7 = '007' EQ; 99P (an integer item) = '12' EQ / '120' NE (temporary of the item's two-character size); ND = ALL '7' NE; literal -7 = '007' NE; ND = SPACES NE. q1grp.cob (run): numeric vs GROUP takes the group move (no conversion, sign byte moved): SIGN SEPARATE -7 = group '-007' EQ, overpunch -7 = group '007' NE and = group holding its raw bytes EQ, while against elementary '007' EQ. Every refused class refused, every admitted class admitted with the comparison the text defines. cite.py: OK §1985:VI.6.3.1.1.2 SR3 [A noninteger numeric operand cannot be compared to a nonnumeric operand]; OK §1985:VI.6.19.4 GR4a [that character is not moved and the size of the sending operand is considered to be one less]; OK §1985:IV.4.3.8.3.3 SR4 [may be used only in an arithmetic expression].
